admission.contract: A connection request is admitted into PROXY v2 parsing when proxy parsing is enabled and execution enters `parse_proxy_protocol_v2` on the request buffer.
limitations: This observation starts after dispatcher selection; it does not independently prove more than the caller's first-4-byte v2 signature match.
Whether deployment enables `proxy_protocol` is configuration-dependent and not derivable from the issue text alone.

root.contract: The parser treats a PROXY v2-prefixed request as complete even though the PROXY v2 header size it computes exceeds the bytes actually read into the request buffer.
root.predicate: root_finalized.hit && root_size.hit && root_finalized.time < root_size.time && root_finalized.crlfcrlf == root_finalized.buffer_start && root_size.size > root_size.buffer_len
limitations: The binding relies on the leading `\r\n\r\n` bytes of the binary v2 signature satisfying request finalization.
This establishes an undersized-buffer state, not a specific overflow write mechanism.

target.contract: After advancing by a PROXY v2 size larger than the received buffer, the parser calls `memmem` on a range whose computed size underflows past the real request buffer end.
limitations: This binds the dangerous consumption to the post-advance `memmem` call; earlier field reads from `hdr` may also consume undersized data but are not separately modeled here.
The predicate infers range underflow from `adjusted_size` exceeding the real buffer length rather than observing allocator or sanitizer effects.
